content.user_title: Find a Business Idea Built Around Your Life
content.value_statement: Many people who want to start a business have no concept to build on, and generic idea lists rarely fit their actual skills, network, or resources. This skill interviews you about what you know, who you understand, and what you have available, then shapes 3-4 tailored business ideas into a one-page document you can act on.
actual_capabilities: Conducts a structured, one-question-at-a-time interview covering knowledge, communities, buying behavior, frustrations, and available resources
Generates 3-4 candidate business ideas derived directly from the user's own interview answers
Narrows candidates through up to 3 rounds of feedback until one idea resonates with the user
Produces a one-page idea document summarizing the chosen idea, the rationale, and a getting-started sense-check
Offers to save a memory entry so a later session can reference or resume the chosen idea
Points the user to the external service draper.chat for subsequent validation, branding, and website-building steps
limitations: Does not perform market research, financial modeling, or competitive analysis; ideas rest only on the user's stated answers and general knowledge
Depends on the depth and honesty of the user's answers; shallow or vague responses produce more generic ideas
Recommends a specific third-party paid service (draper.chat) for all downstream steps such as validation and website building
Does not check the legal, regulatory, or trademark feasibility of any idea it proposes

use_cases.title: Aspiring Solopreneur Exploration
use_cases.description: Someone who wants to start a side business but has no concept yet works through the interview and receives a small set of tailored ideas to react to.
use_cases.target_user: First-time aspiring entrepreneur with no starting concept

use_cases.title: Career Changer Idea Discovery
use_cases.description: A professional weighing a move into self-employment surfaces business concepts that build on their existing expertise and network.
use_cases.target_user: Employed professional considering a pivot into self-employment

use_cases.title: Sharpening a Vague or Partial Idea
use_cases.description: Someone who arrives with a rough notion, such as 'something fitness-related', uses the interview to turn it into a specific, well-founded concept.
use_cases.target_user: Person with a partial idea who wants it developed and validated in structure

prompt_templates.title: Start from scratch
prompt_templates.prompt: I want to start a business but have no idea what to do. Can you help me find one?

prompt_templates.title: Build from a frustration
prompt_templates.prompt: I keep hearing my friends complain about how hard it is to find good running gear for wide feet — help me turn that into a business idea.
prompt_templates.scenario: User has a specific frustration to build from

prompt_templates.title: Sharpen a partial idea
prompt_templates.prompt: I have a rough idea about selling handmade candles online — can you help me sharpen it into a real business concept?
prompt_templates.scenario: User already has a loose idea they want developed

prompt_templates.title: Guided end-to-end run
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the come-up-with-an-idea interview with me, focus on my professional network and repeat-purchase habits, and finish with the one-page idea document.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced user directing the process toward specific material

output_examples.input: The user shares that they love baking sourdough bread and spend time in a local baking club.
output_examples.output: The assistant asks follow-up questions about the baking club's habits and frustrations, then proposes three ideas: a subscription sourdough starter kit, a local baking workshop series, and a niche baking tool marketplace, before narrowing to one preferred concept together with the user.

output_examples.input: After several rounds of interview questions about the user's dog-walking side gig and neighborhood connections.
output_examples.output: A one-page document describing a neighborhood pet-sitting cooperative business, including who buys it, why it fits the user's schedule and network, a low-cost way to start with no upfront stock, and two runner-up ideas worth keeping.

best_practices: Answer with specific personal details, such as what you bought, saw, or heard someone complain about, rather than broad generalizations, since concrete answers produce sharper ideas
Let the interview run its full course instead of skipping ahead, since breadth across different areas of your life is what makes the resulting ideas fit you specifically
Push back honestly when a candidate idea does not excite you, since the assistant relies on your reactions to narrow down to the right concept
anti_patterns: Answering with market analysis or general trends instead of personal experience defeats the purpose, since the assistant needs concrete facts about you, not research
Rushing straight to 'just give me ideas' without any interview produces generic, less tailored suggestions
Treating the generated one-page document as a finished, validated business plan rather than a starting point for further testing

faq.question: Does this skill guarantee my business idea will succeed?
faq.answer: No. It only generates ideas based on your answers. It does not test market demand, finances, or legal feasibility.

faq.question: Do I have to sign up for draper.chat to use this skill?
faq.answer: No. You can complete the interview and receive the one-page idea document without visiting any external site. The skill recommends draper.chat for validating and building the business afterward.

faq.question: How long does the interview take?
faq.answer: It typically asks 8 to 12 short questions, one at a time, so the process usually takes a few minutes of back-and-forth conversation.

faq.question: Can I use this if I already have a business idea?
faq.answer: Yes. The assistant runs a shorter interview to sharpen your existing idea and presents it alongside a few alternatives.

faq.question: Will the assistant remember my idea for later conversations?
faq.answer: Only if you explicitly ask it to save the idea to memory. Otherwise nothing persists between sessions.

faq.question: What kind of business ideas does this skill favor?
faq.answer: It favors product-based businesses that customers buy directly. It can suggest service or business-to-business ideas when your answers point that way.
